system:
You audit the knowledge atoms of one Knowledge Card. A card is the answer key for a benchmark of expert conceptual knowledge, so every atom must be correct, self-contained, and assessable on its own.

Judge every atom on every check listed below. Rules:
- For checks about evidence, use only the evidence sentences supplied with the atom. Do not repair an atom with your own knowledge.
- Evidence text comes from a PDF text layer. If symbols are garbled so that you cannot verify the atom, answer "hold" for that check and say so.
- Be strict. When unsure between pass and a non-pass value, choose the non-pass value and explain.
- "why" is required for every value other than the first listed value; keep it under 30 words. Omit "why" when passing.

Checks (allowed values in brackets; the first value means no problem):
- GROUNDED [pass / revise / fail]: The cited evidence sentences state the atom. pass = fully stated. revise = the core claim is stated, and the gap is only wording, strength, or a dropped/extra peripheral qualifier that can be fixed by deleting or softening words (say what). fail = not stated, OR the atom adds substantive content the evidence lacks: a scope or population restriction (e.g. 'In B-ALL'), a mechanism or operation, a characterization (e.g. 'an unbounded while loop'), or a formula/definition. If deleting the unsupported part would change what the atom tests, it is fail, not revise. For pass, put the supporting evidence ids in cite (required).
- SINGLE_CLAIM [pass / revise]: The atom is one independently assessable claim. revise = it joins two or more claims that could be true or false separately.
- SCOPE_LABEL [pass / revise]: The S label fits (S1 what it is / S2 how it works / S3 where it ends). revise = wrong label; put the right one in why, e.g. 'S2: ...'.
- L1_ONLY [pass / revise / fail]: The atom is recall-level knowledge: one fact a person who studied the concept would simply know. revise = the core fact is recall-level but the sentence carries extra load that must be removed, e.g. stacked conditions (since/although/if ... and ...), a procedural or evaluative add-on ('easy to define but requires checking ...'), or a clause that introduces a second technical concept that must be known separately (e.g. 'if X is an inner Kan complex' when that is not the card concept). fail = knowing it requires applying the concept to a new problem, or combining facts from distant passages.
- SOURCE_INDEPENDENT [pass / revise / fail]: A domain expert who never read this book could judge the claim true or false. revise = phrased as the authors' statement but the claim itself is general (drop the attribution). fail = the authors' opinion or choice, or the finding of one study, so the answer is not fixed without the source.
- NO_OVERLAP [pass / fail]: No other atom in this card states or contains the same claim. If two atoms overlap, fail only the less informative one and put the other atom's id in cite; the other one passes.
- CENTRALITY [pass / fail]: The atom matters for understanding the concept. fail = peripheral detail.
Whole-card checks (report under "batch"):
- CONCEPT_SCOPE [pass / fail]: The concept is a general concept of the field. fail = a single system, product, or one study's topic.

Output ONLY one JSON object:
{"units": {"<atom_id>": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": "", "cite": []}, ...}, ...}, "batch": {"<CHECK>": {"v": "<value>", "why": ""}}}

CONCEPT: Anodyne morphism
ASSESSMENT SCOPE: Left-lifting-property definition with respect to Kan/inner/left/right fibrations (and dendroidal leaf/root variants), characterization as saturation of horn inclusions via retracts of cellular maps, generalized horns Λ^E, and spine criteria. Excludes pushout-product lemmas.

ATOMS:
- HMDEND-C06-S1-01 | S1
  ATOM: An inner, left, or right anodyne morphism of simplicial sets is defined as a morphism having the left lifting property with respect to inner, left, or right fibrations, respectively.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0190-s22] Definition 5.16 An anodyne morphism of simplicial sets is a morphism having the left lifting property with respect to all Kan fibrations.
- HMDEND-C06-S1-02.r1a | S1
  ATOM: An anodyne morphism of dendroidal sets is a morphism that has the left lifting property with respect to all dendroidal Kan fibrations.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0240-s10] Definition 6.14 An anodyne morphism of dendroidal sets is a morphism having the left lifting property with respect to all dendroidal Kan fibrations.
- HMDEND-C06-S1-02.r1b | S1
  ATOM: An inner, leaf, or root anodyne morphism of dendroidal sets is a morphism that has the left lifting property with respect to inner, left, or right fibrations, respectively.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0240-s11] Similarly, an inner, leaf, or root anodyne morphism is a morphism having the left lifting property with respect to inner, left, or right fibrations, respectively.
- HMDEND-C06-S2-01.r1a | S2
  ATOM: A map of simplicial sets is anodyne if and only if it is a retract of an $\mathcal{I}$-cellular map, where $\mathcal{I}$ is the set of horn inclusions $\Lambda^k[n]\to\Delta[n]$.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0191-s18] Lemma 5.20 A map f : A →B of simplicial sets is anodyne if and only it is a retract of an I-cellular map, with I the set of horn inclusions Λk[n] →∆[n].
- HMDEND-C06-S2-01.r1b | S2
  ATOM: A map of simplicial sets is inner, left, or right anodyne if and only if it is a retract of a map that is cellular with respect to the inner, left, or right horn inclusions respectively.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0191-s19] Similarly it is inner, left, or right anodyne if and only if it is a retract of a map which is cellular with respect to inner, left, or right horn inclusions respectively.
- HMDEND-C06-S2-02 | S2
  ATOM: The class of anodyne maps of simplicial sets is the smallest saturated class containing the horn inclusions, and likewise for inner, left, and right anodyne maps with their respective horn inclusions, so anodynes form the saturation of the horn inclusions.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0192-s02] Corollary 5.21 The class of (inner, left, or right) anodyne maps is the smallest saturated class containing the (inner, left, or right) horn inclusions.
    [HMDEND-p0192-s04] For this reason, we will sometimes refer to the class of (inner, left, or right)
    [HMDEND-p0192-s05] anodynes as the saturation of the class of (inner, left, or right) horn inclusions.
- HMDEND-C06-S2-03.r1a | S2
  ATOM: For a tree $T$ and a non-empty subset $E$ of its inner edges, the inclusion $\Lambda^E[T]\to\Omega[T]$, where $\Lambda^E[T]$ is the union of those faces of $T$ that contain all the inner edges in $E$, is a composition of pushouts of inner horn inclusions.
  EVIDENCE:

    [HMDEND-p0241-s08] In other words, ΛE[T] is the union of those faces of T which contain all the inner edges in the set E.
    [HMDEND-p0241-s09] Then the inclusion ΛE[T] →Ω[T] is a composition of pushouts of inner horn inclusions.
- HMDEND-C06-S2-03.r1b | S2
  ATOM: For a tree $T$ and a non-empty subset $E$ of its inner edges, the inclusion $\Lambda^E[T]\to\Omega[T]$ is an inner anodyne morphism.
  EVIDENCE:
    [HMDEND-p0241-s06] Lemma 6.20 Let T be a tree and let E be a non-empty subset of the set I(T) of inner edges.
    [HMDEND-p0241-s09] Then the inclusion ΛE[T] →Ω[T] is a composition of pushouts of inner horn inclusions.
    [HMDEND-p0241-s10] In particular it is an inner anodyne morphism.

  ATOM: A saturated class of normal monomorphisms between dendroidal sets contains all inner anodyne morphisms if it contains all spine inclusions of trees and satisfies this closure property: for monomorphisms $i:A\to B$ and $j:B\to C$ with $i$ and $ji$ in the class, $j$ is also in the class.
